Topic 3.3: Domestic Animals

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Domestic Animals, part of Our Home 3.2 Work Done at Home (10 lessons) By the end of the Sub Strand, the le in SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we have animals at home? 2. How can we care for domestic animals at home?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Domestic Animals together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy: as learner manipulates and interacts with digital devices with assistive technology to watch or listen to videos on domestic

animals.

Values:
Love: learner enhances caring skills when feeding domestic animals.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Animal welfare education: learner enhances environmental awareness as they go for a nature walk to observe domestic animals.

Link to other learning area:

Domestic animals relates to the concept of creation in Religious Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

Charts, picture cards, flash cards, braille cards, glue, crayons, coloured pencils, video clips, clay, plasticine, photos, tactile diagrams, braille

cards of names of different domestic animals, braille writing materials and equipment.
